title: Keep punctuation with its sentence
statement: When words in a sentence become answer choices, blanks or glossary buttons, keep the sentence's punctuation attached to its word or final choice, and check wrapping before and after selection.
example: One staging sweep recorded 13 places where a sentence's comma or full stop fell alone onto a line below the answer choices.
detail: Sentence-final full stops and commas fell onto a line of their own below groups of answer chips, 13 times in one staging sweep, and once after a glossary button at the end of a passage sentence, where the button and the full stop were separate elements. A fix confirmed on the one page first reported did not cover the other sentence-completion layouts. The repair direction keeps trailing punctuation with its sentence or selected ending and checks wrapping before and after a selection.
against: A later laptop sweep did not reproduce it at 1100 × 700 on the four pages where the staging sweep had seen it at that width, and limits its own claim: "No claim about other widths." (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/laptop-student-sweep/README.md`, lines 60-61).

evidence.quote: The sentence-final period renders alone on a new line below the answer options, visibly detached from the sentence.
Repair direction: keep trailing punctuation with its sentence/selected ending instead of leaving it after a block of choices. Verify wrapping before and after a selection.
Expected: punctuation should stay attached to the sentence or final chip rather than occupy a separate line.
This is the same defect family as earlier main finding V3, on additional staging pages. The previously sampled V3 fix does not cover all sentence-completion layouts.
Additional occurrences visually observed in the sweep (each has a saved image; the three above received dedicated re-navigation reproductions):
DOM evidence: the final glossary button uses class 'bk-gw' inside a 'bk-seek' span, followed by a separate period text node.
